title: Complex Offshore Structures & International Finance Solution
summary: Service page (Residential / Wealth menu) on arranging finance where the borrowing or ownership structure is atypical: multiple borrowing entities and SPVs, cross-border and offshore assets, layered debt with intercreditor arrangements, and trust-, foundation- and estate-held assets. The page states that traditional high street lenders generally prefer not to lend on such transactions, that many traditional lenders cannot get comfortable with complex offshore assets and ownership structures, and that Silver Oak Capital has a network of 'hundreds of offshore lenders who specialise in this type of lending'. It advises giving the lender a clear, simple structure chart early and says the firm has advised on trust- and estate-held assets, onshore and offshore. Search snippets only; full page text, H1, meta description, pricing, LTV and process details were not revealed. Related site content (FAQ, BVI trust refinance case study, private bank mortgages page) was surfaced and is recorded with tags.

sections.heading: Related site content (not on this page)
sections.content: [a][b] FAQ: a 'complex' structure is any atypical one; complex finance is sometimes more expensive, depending on the degree of complexity, the borrower type, and the risk profile of the security. [b] Private bank mortgages page: 'Charges over trusts, special purpose vehicles and companies are also common forms of security form private banks. While they are very seldom the only security a private bank will take, they are often included in the overall security package.' [b] BVI trust refinance case study: UK landlord's property held in a British Virgin Islands trust, trustees based in Guernsey; matched with a private bank that had a BVI office; £5 million, 2.75% fixed for five years, interest-only over 10 years, personal guarantee; 'The lender also needed a good working relationship with the trustees (based in Guernsey).'
